manifest.title: Graphs of twin-width at most 2 have bounded mim-width

inputs.abstract:
Every graph of twin-width at most $2$ has mim-width at most $8$. Given a $2$-sequence, a polynomial-time word-RAM algorithm constructs a branch decomposition witnessing the bound. This yields polynomial-time algorithms for fixed-$k$ Coloring, four domination problems, Weighted Feedback Vertex Set, Subset Feedback Vertex Set, and Longest Induced Path.

For $t \ge 2$, an $n$-vertex graph of twin-width at most $2$ with no induced $K_{t,t}$ has tree-independence number at most $84(t-1)$. Given a $2$-sequence, a word RAM constructs a tree decomposition meeting this bound in $n^{O(t)}$ time.

When the number of colors is part of the input, Minimum Coloring is NP-complete even when a $2$-sequence is supplied.

concepts.title: The auxiliary tree of a 2-sequence
concepts.description:
Move each fringe of a red edge to the neighboring part, then group the parts
in the red components left after deleting the selected edges. The resulting
partitions refine one another. Suppressing repetitions gives a rooted tree.
Its internal nodes have between 2 and 5 children. Every cut below a node is
covered by at most 4 chain subgraphs (Lemmas 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, and 3.10).

In the prefix encoding, an original fork has tag $0$ and a fork added to
write a node with more than 2 children has tag $1$. A leaf with vertex
number $v$ is written as $v+2$. Contracting the added forks recovers the
auxiliary tree.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.ChainCuts
import Lax759944.RamPolytime

/-!
---
title: The auxiliary tree of a 2-sequence
type: lemma
---
Move each fringe of a red edge to the neighboring part, then group the parts
in the red components left after deleting the selected edges. The resulting
partitions refine one another. Suppressing repetitions gives a rooted tree.
Its internal nodes have between 2 and 5 children. Every cut below a node is
covered by at most 4 chain subgraphs (Lemmas 3.5, 3.7, 3.9, and 3.10).

In the prefix encoding, an original fork has tag $0$ and a fork added to
write a node with more than 2 children has tag $1$. A leaf with vertex
number $v$ is written as $v+2$. Contracting the added forks recovers the
auxiliary tree.
-/

namespace Lax528502.AuxiliaryTree

open Lax183560 Lax228581.TwinWidth Lax759944.RamPolytime

inductive Tree (V : Type)
  | leaf (v : V)
  | two (a b : Tree V)
  | three (a b c : Tree V)
  | four (a b c d : Tree V)
  | five (a b c d e : Tree V)

variable {V : Type}

open BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree in
/-- Resolve every node into binary forks. At a node with 5 children, the
parent edge and the first child form one of the 3 pairs of incident edges. -/
def Tree.refine : Tree V → BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree V
  | .leaf v => .leaf v
  | .two a b => fork a.refine b.refine
  | .three a b c => fork a.refine (fork b.refine c.refine)
  | .four a b c d => fork (fork a.refine b.refine) (fork c.refine d.refine)
  | .five a b c d e => fork a.refine (fork (fork b.refine c.refine) (fork d.refine e.refine))

/-- The vertices below the root of this subtree. -/
def Tree.support [DecidableEq V] (h : Tree V) : Finset V := h.refine.leaves.toFinset

/-- A predicate holds below every node, including the root. -/
def Tree.All (P : Tree V → Prop) : Tree V → Prop
  | h@(.leaf _) => P h
  | h@(.two a b) => P h ∧ a.All P ∧ b.All P
  | h@(.three a b c) => P h ∧ a.All P ∧ b.All P ∧ c.All P
  | h@(.four a b c d) => P h ∧ a.All P ∧ b.All P ∧ c.All P ∧ d.All P
  | h@(.five a b c d e) => P h ∧ a.All P ∧ b.All P ∧ c.All P ∧ d.All P ∧ e.All P

/-- A hierarchy of the vertex set together with the 4-chain property at each cut. -/
def Certified [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Option (Tree V) → Prop
  | none => IsEmpty V
  | some h => h.refine.Valid Finset.univ ∧ h.All fun s => Nonempty (ChainCuts.Cover G s.support 4)

def Tree.word {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V) : Tree V → List ℕ
  | .leaf v => [(order.symm v).val + 2]
  | .two a b => 0 :: a.word order ++ b.word order
  | .three a b c => 0 :: a.word order ++ [1] ++ b.word order ++ c.word order
  | .four a b c d => [0, 1] ++ a.word order ++ b.word order ++ [1] ++ c.word order ++ d.word order
  | .five a b c d e =>
      0 :: a.word order ++ [1, 1] ++ b.word order ++ c.word order ++ [1] ++ d.word order ++ e.word order

def encode {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V) (h : Option (Tree V)) : List ℕ :=
  h.elim [] (Tree.word order)

/-- Construct the auxiliary tree in polynomial time from the 2-sequence. -/
axiom construct :
    ∃ build : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime build ∧
      ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V)
        (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2),
        ∃ h, Certified G h ∧ build (ContractionInput.encode order G S) = encode order h

end Lax528502.AuxiliaryTree

concepts.title: Resolving the auxiliary tree into a branch decomposition
concepts.description:
An auxiliary node has degree at most 6. Partition its incident edges into
groups of size at most 2 and attach the groups to a central node. Each new
cut has one side equal to the union of at most 2 old sides. Its induced
matching number is at most $4+4=8$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.AuxiliaryTree

/-!
---
title: Resolving the auxiliary tree into a branch decomposition
type: lemma
---
An auxiliary node has degree at most 6. Partition its incident edges into
groups of size at most 2 and attach the groups to a central node. Each new
cut has one side equal to the union of at most 2 old sides. Its induced
matching number is at most $4+4=8$.
-/

namespace Lax528502.BinaryRefinement

open AuxiliaryTree

axiom width_le_eight {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (h : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)) (hc : Certified G h) :
    MimWidth.Decomposes G 8 (h.map AuxiliaryTree.Tree.refine)

end Lax528502.BinaryRefinement

concepts.title: Algorithms supplied with a bounded-mim-width decomposition
concepts.description:
For fixed width $w$, the domination and fixed-color algorithms of Bergougnoux,
Dreier, and Jaffke, the induced-path and weighted feedback vertex set
algorithms of Jaffke, Kwon, and Telle, and the subset feedback vertex set
algorithm of Bergougnoux, Papadopoulos, and Telle take polynomial time given
a branch decomposition of width at most $w$.

The graph is the initial adjacency matrix on the input. A polynomial-time
subroutine supplies the encoded decomposition. The assertions apply wherever
the returned tree is valid. Framing the auxiliary data separately lets the
same subroutine handle all 7 optimization problems.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.ContractionInput
import Lax528502.MimWidth
import Lax528502.GraphProblems
import Lax759944.RamPolytime

/-!
---
title: Algorithms supplied with a bounded-mim-width decomposition
type: theorem
---
For fixed width $w$, the domination and fixed-color algorithms of Bergougnoux,
Dreier, and Jaffke, the induced-path and weighted feedback vertex set
algorithms of Jaffke, Kwon, and Telle, and the subset feedback vertex set
algorithm of Bergougnoux, Papadopoulos, and Telle take polynomial time given
a branch decomposition of width at most $w$.

The graph is the initial adjacency matrix on the input. A polynomial-time
subroutine supplies the encoded decomposition. The assertions apply wherever
the returned tree is valid. Framing the auxiliary data separately lets the
same subroutine handle all 7 optimization problems.
-/

namespace Lax528502.BoundedMimAlgorithms

open Lax759944.RamPolytime Lax183560 GraphProblems

/-- A polynomial-time branch-decomposition routine suffices for fixed-color decision. -/
axiom fixedColoring (w k : ℕ) (branch : List ℕ → List ℕ) (hb : RamPolytime branch) :
    ∃ solve : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime solve ∧
      ∀ (x : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree (Fin n))),
        (ContractionInput.graph (Equiv.refl _) G).IsPrefix x →
        branch x = MimWidth.encode (Equiv.refl _) T → MimWidth.Decomposes G w T →
        ∃ b : Bool, solve x = [b.toNat] ∧ (b = true ↔ G.Colorable k)

/-- The three domination variants that allow the selected set to be disconnected. -/
axiom domination (w : ℕ) (branch : List ℕ → List ℕ) (hb : RamPolytime branch) :
    ∃ solve : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime solve ∧
      ∀ (x : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree (Fin n))),
        (ContractionInput.graph (Equiv.refl _) G).IsPrefix x →
        branch x = MimWidth.encode (Equiv.refl _) T → MimWidth.Decomposes G w T →
        ∀ P : Problem n, (P = .dominating ∨ P = .totalDominating ∨ P = .independentDominating) →
          P.Answer G (solve (input x P))

/-- A polynomial-time branch-decomposition routine suffices to find a minimum connected dominating set. -/
axiom connectedDominating (w : ℕ) (branch : List ℕ → List ℕ) (hb : RamPolytime branch) :
    ∃ solve : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime solve ∧
      ∀ (x : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree (Fin n))),
        (ContractionInput.graph (Equiv.refl _) G).IsPrefix x →
        branch x = MimWidth.encode (Equiv.refl _) T → MimWidth.Decomposes G w T →
        Problem.connectedDominating.Answer G (solve x)

/-- A polynomial-time branch-decomposition routine suffices to find a longest induced path. -/
axiom longestInducedPath (w : ℕ) (branch : List ℕ → List ℕ) (hb : RamPolytime branch) :
    ∃ solve : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime solve ∧
      ∀ (x : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree (Fin n))),
        (ContractionInput.graph (Equiv.refl _) G).IsPrefix x →
        branch x = MimWidth.encode (Equiv.refl _) T → MimWidth.Decomposes G w T →
        Problem.longestInducedPath.Answer G (solve x)

/-- A common word RAM minimizes deletion weight or hits all cycles through a marked vertex set. -/
axiom feedback (w : ℕ) (branch : List ℕ → List ℕ) (hb : RamPolytime branch) :
    ∃ solve : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime solve ∧
      ∀ (x : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree (Fin n))),
        (ContractionInput.graph (Equiv.refl _) G).IsPrefix x →
        branch x = MimWidth.encode (Equiv.refl _) T → MimWidth.Decomposes G w T →
        (∀ cost : Fin n → ℕ, (Problem.weightedFeedback cost).Answer G (solve (input x (.weightedFeedback cost)))) ∧
        (∀ marked : Finset (Fin n), (Problem.subsetFeedback marked).Answer G (solve (input x (.subsetFeedback marked))))

/-- A common solver for every optimization problem in the corollary. -/
axiom optimization (w : ℕ) (branch : List ℕ → List ℕ) (hb : RamPolytime branch) :
    ∃ solve : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime solve ∧
      ∀ (x : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree (Fin n))),
        (ContractionInput.graph (Equiv.refl _) G).IsPrefix x →
        branch x = MimWidth.encode (Equiv.refl _) T → MimWidth.Decomposes G w T →
        ∀ P : Problem n, P.Answer G (solve (input x P))

end Lax528502.BoundedMimAlgorithms

concepts.title: Covers of a cut by chain graphs
concepts.description:
A chain subgraph of a cut has nested neighborhoods on one side. If $r$ chain
subgraphs cover all crossing edges, any induced matching across the cut has
size at most $r$.

For the tree-independence bound, put $K=r(t-1)$. Let $H_X$ consist of the
vertices outside $X$ with an independent set of more than $K$ neighbors in
$X$. Let $I_X$ consist of the vertices in $X$ adjacent to an outside vertex
outside $H_X$. The two sets cover the cut. When $G$ excludes an induced
$K_{t,t}$, their independence numbers are at most $K$ and $rK$, respectively
(Lemma 4.2).
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.MimWidth
import Lax528502.TreeIndependence

/-!
---
title: Covers of a cut by chain graphs
type: lemma
---
A chain subgraph of a cut has nested neighborhoods on one side. If $r$ chain
subgraphs cover all crossing edges, any induced matching across the cut has
size at most $r$.

For the tree-independence bound, put $K=r(t-1)$. Let $H_X$ consist of the
vertices outside $X$ with an independent set of more than $K$ neighbors in
$X$. Let $I_X$ consist of the vertices in $X$ adjacent to an outside vertex
outside $H_X$. The two sets cover the cut. When $G$ excludes an induced
$K_{t,t}$, their independence numbers are at most $K$ and $rK$, respectively
(Lemma 4.2).
-/

namespace Lax528502.ChainCuts

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- The neighborhoods of vertices of Y in X are linearly ordered by inclusion. -/
def ChainOn (G : SimpleGraph V) (X Y : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∀ y ∈ Y, ∀ z ∈ Y,
    (∀ x ∈ X, G.Adj x y → G.Adj x z) ∨ (∀ x ∈ X, G.Adj x z → G.Adj x y)

/-- For each chain and outside vertex, specify its neighbors on the inside. -/
structure Cover (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Finset V) (r : ℕ) where
  neighbors : Fin r → V → Finset V
  sound : ∀ j v u, u ∈ neighbors j v → u ∈ X ∧ v ∉ X ∧ G.Adj u v
  nested : ∀ j v w, neighbors j v ⊆ neighbors j w ∨ neighbors j w ⊆ neighbors j v
  covers : ∀ u ∈ X, ∀ v ∉ X, G.Adj u v → ∃ j, u ∈ neighbors j v

/-- A cut covered by r chain graphs has induced matching number at most r. -/
axiom cutMim_le {G : SimpleGraph V} {X : Finset V} {r : ℕ}
    (C : Cover G X r) : MimWidth.cutMim G X ≤ r

/-- The outside vertices with a large independent set of neighbors inside. -/
noncomputable def heavy (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Finset V) (k : ℕ) : Finset V := by
  classical
  exact Xᶜ.filter fun v => ∃ A ⊆ X, G.IsIndepSet (A : Set V) ∧ k < A.card ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, G.Adj a v

/-- Inside endpoints of cut edges with an outside endpoint outside H. -/
noncomputable def inside (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Finset V) (k : ℕ) : Finset V := by
  classical
  exact X.filter fun u => ∃ v ∉ X, v ∉ heavy G X k ∧ G.Adj u v

/-- The independence bounds for the two sides of the cut cover. -/
axiom independence_bounds {G : SimpleGraph V} {X : Finset V} {r t : ℕ}
    (C : Cover G X r) (ht : 2 ≤ t) (hfree : TreeIndependence.InducedBicliqueFree G t) :
    let K := r * (t - 1)
    (∀ A ⊆ heavy G X K, G.IsIndepSet (A : Set V) → A.card ≤ K) ∧
    (∀ A ⊆ inside G X K, G.IsIndepSet (A : Set V) → A.card ≤ r * K)

end Lax528502.ChainCuts

concepts.title: The ordered-clique graph and its contraction sequence
concepts.description:
The disjoint paths reduction assigns a position to each vertex and each arc,
and one extra position to the dummy vertex. Incoming and outgoing arcs are
processed in topological order by optional exchanges of two positions.
Copies of the ordered cliques align each modified crossing edge with a block
boundary. After deleting the dummy, merge the prefixes of the blocks from
right to left and then contract consecutive blocks (Section 5).
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.DisjointPaths
import Lax528502.ColoringGadgets

/-!
---
title: The ordered-clique graph and its contraction sequence
type: lemma
---
The disjoint paths reduction assigns a position to each vertex and each arc,
and one extra position to the dummy vertex. Incoming and outgoing arcs are
processed in topological order by optional exchanges of two positions.
Copies of the ordered cliques align each modified crossing edge with a block
boundary. After deleting the dummy, merge the prefixes of the blocks from
right to left and then contract consecutive blocks (Section 5).
-/

namespace Lax528502.CliqueConstruction

open ColoringGadgets

abbrev Step := EdgePattern ℕ

/-- Exchange p and q optionally, restoring every intermediate position. -/
def exchange (p q : ℕ) : List Step :=
  let moves := (List.range (q - p - 1)).map fun i =>
    EdgePattern.swap (p + i) (p + i + 1)
  moves ++ [.choice (q - 1) q] ++ moves.reverse

structure Plan where
  colors : ℕ
  steps : List Step

/-- Number sources, sinks, and old vertices, add private terminal arcs, and
process the vertices in a topological order. All positions start at 0. -/
def plan (n : ℕ) (arcs terminals : List (ℕ × ℕ)) : Plan :=
  let pairs := terminals.zipIdx
  let old := fun v => 2 * terminals.length + v
  let vertices := pairs.map (fun (_, h) => 2*h) ++ (List.range n).map old ++
    pairs.map (fun (_, h) => 2*h+1)
  let edges := pairs.map (fun ((s,_), h) => (2*h, old s)) ++
    arcs.map (fun (u,v) => (old u, old v)) ++ pairs.map (fun ((_,t), h) => (old t, 2*h+1))
  let indexed := edges.zipIdx
  let transfers := fun v (arcsAtVertex : List ((ℕ × ℕ) × ℕ)) =>
    arcsAtVertex.flatMap fun (_, i) => exchange v (vertices.length + i)
  let route := vertices.flatMap fun v =>
    transfers v (indexed.filter fun ((_,t), _) => t == v) ++
      transfers v (indexed.filter fun ((s,_), _) => s == v)
  let active := vertices.length + edges.length
  let free := (List.range active).filter fun p => !(p < 2 * pairs.length && p % 2 == 1)
  let permute := free.flatMap fun p => (free.filter (p < ·)).flatMap (exchange p)
  let swaps := pairs.map fun (_, h) => EdgePattern.swap (2*h) (2*h+1)
  ⟨active + 1, .copy :: route ++ permute ++ swaps⟩

/-- Insert at least one copy before each operation and at the closing edge.
If the left position is p, the new column has index p+2 modulo m=k−1. -/
def pad (m previous : ℕ) : List Step → List Step
  | [] => List.replicate (m - previous % m) .copy
  | step :: rest =>
    let copies := match step with
      | .copy => 1
      | .swap p _ | .choice p _ => 1 + (p % m + (m - previous % m)) % m
    List.replicate copies .copy ++ step :: pad m (previous + copies + 1) rest

/-- Check the congruence of every special step and of the total column count. -/
def Aligned (m previous : ℕ) : List Step → Prop
  | [] => previous % m = 0
  | .copy :: xs => Aligned m (previous + 1) xs
  | .swap p _ :: xs | .choice p _ :: xs =>
    (previous + 1) % m = (p + 2) % m ∧ Aligned m (previous + 1) xs

/-- Padding places every modified crossing edge at the prescribed block boundary. -/
axiom padding_aligns (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (previous : ℕ) (ops : List Step) :
    Aligned m previous (pad m previous ops)

/-- Delete the dummy vertex of column 0 and use the vertex numbering C−1. -/
def vertexCount (k : ℕ) (steps : List Step) : ℕ := k * (steps.length + 1) - 1

def graph (k : ℕ) (steps : List Step) : SimpleGraph (Fin (vertexCount k steps)) :=
  let column := fun (v : Fin (vertexCount k steps)) => (v.val + 1) / k
  let position := fun (v : Fin (vertexCount k steps)) => k - 1 - ((v.val + 1) % k)
  let forward := fun u v =>
    (column v = column u + 1 ∧ (steps[column u]?.getD .copy).Edge (position u) (position v)) ∨
    (column u = steps.length ∧ column v = 0 ∧ position u < position v)
  { Adj := fun u v => u ≠ v ∧ (column u = column v ∨ forward u v ∨ forward v u)
    symm := ⟨fun _ _ ⟨hne, h⟩ => ⟨hne.symm, h.elim (fun e => Or.inl e.symm)
      (fun e => Or.inr e.symm)⟩⟩
    loopless := ⟨fun _ h => h.1 rfl⟩ }

/-- The pair (a,b) means that the part represented by b joins the part
represented by a. First grow every block prefix, then merge adjacent blocks. -/
def merges (blockSize blocks : ℕ) : List (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  let grow := (List.range (blockSize - 1)).flatMap fun j =>
    (List.range blocks).reverse.map fun i => (blockSize*i, blockSize*i+j+1)
  grow ++ (List.range (blocks - 1)).map fun i => (0, blockSize*(i+1))

def representative (ms : List (ℕ × ℕ)) (v : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ms.foldl (fun part (a,b) => if part = b then a else part) v

/-- Serialize the graph, followed by the equivalence matrix after every
prefix of the merge list, in the coloring input format. -/
noncomputable def Plan.words (P : Plan) : List ℕ :=
  let k := P.colors
  let steps := pad (k-1) 0 P.steps
  let n := vertexCount k steps
  let ms := merges (k-1) (n / (k-1))
  let partitions := (List.range (ms.length + 1)).flatMap fun i =>
    let rep := representative (ms.take i)
    ContractionInput.matrix n n fun u v => rep u.val = rep v.val
  k :: ContractionInput.graph (Equiv.refl _) (graph k steps) ++ [ms.length] ++ partitions

/-- The graph, color count, and explicit 2-sequence prescribed on a DAG input. -/
noncomputable def words (I : DisjointPaths.Instance) : List ℕ := by
  classical
  let arcs := (List.ofFn fun (u : Fin I.n) => (List.ofFn id).filterMap fun v =>
    if I.arc u v then some (u.val,v.val) else none).flatten
  exact (plan I.n arcs (I.terminals.map fun (s,t) => (s.val,t.val))).words

end Lax528502.CliqueConstruction

concepts.title: Color propagation between ordered cliques
concepts.description:
In a proper $k$-coloring, each ordered $k$-clique uses every color once.
Between consecutive cliques, the copy gadget forces their color orders to
agree. The swap gadget forces an adjacent transposition. The choice gadget
allows either order (Lemma 5.1).
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.GroupTheory.Perm.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Basic

/-!
---
title: Color propagation between ordered cliques
type: lemma
---
In a proper $k$-coloring, each ordered $k$-clique uses every color once.
Between consecutive cliques, the copy gadget forces their color orders to
agree. The swap gadget forces an adjacent transposition. The choice gadget
allows either order (Lemma 5.1).
-/

namespace Lax528502.ColoringGadgets

/-- Two consecutive positions in a clique of size k, numbered from 0. -/
structure Consecutive (k : ℕ) where
  left : Fin k
  right : Fin k
  next : right.val = left.val + 1

inductive Operation (k : ℕ)
  | copy
  | swap (i : Consecutive k)
  | choice (i : Consecutive k)

variable {k : ℕ}

/-- A crossing-edge pattern, on either finite clique positions or their numerical labels. -/
inductive EdgePattern (α : Type)
  | copy
  | swap (left right : α)
  | choice (left right : α)
  deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited

def EdgePattern.Edge {α : Type} [LT α] (op : EdgePattern α) (p q : α) : Prop :=
  match op with
  | .copy => p < q
  | .choice l r => p < q ∧ (p,q) ≠ (l,r)
  | .swap l r => (p < q ∧ (p,q) ≠ (l,r)) ∨ (p,q) = (l,l)

/-- Crossing edges from position p of the old clique to q of the new one. -/
def Operation.Edge (op : Operation k) (p q : Fin k) : Prop :=
  let pattern : EdgePattern (Fin k) := match op with
    | .copy => .copy
    | .swap i => .swap i.left i.right
    | .choice i => .choice i.left i.right
  pattern.Edge p q

/-- The old position carrying the color at each new position is given by π. -/
def Operation.Proper (op : Operation k) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) : Prop :=
  ∀ q, ¬ op.Edge (π q) q

def Operation.Allows (op : Operation k) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) : Prop :=
  match op with
  | .copy => π = Equiv.refl _
  | .swap i => π = Equiv.swap i.left i.right
  | .choice i => π = Equiv.refl _ ∨ π = Equiv.swap i.left i.right

/-- The three gadgets permit exactly the prescribed changes of color order. -/
axiom proper_iff_allows (op : Operation k) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) : op.Proper π ↔ op.Allows π

end Lax528502.ColoringGadgets

concepts.title: Minimum Coloring with a witnessing 2-sequence
concepts.description:
An instance consists of a graph $G$, a positive integer $k$, and a valid
$2$-sequence of $G$. It is accepted if $G$ has a proper $k$-coloring.
The binary language contains exactly the encodings of accepted instances.
The promise consists of the encodings of all instances, including negative ones.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.ContractionInput
import Lax434930.PolynomialTime
import Lax759944.BinaryWordEncoding
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.Vertex

/-!
---
title: Minimum Coloring with a witnessing 2-sequence
type: definition
---
An instance consists of a graph $G$, a positive integer $k$, and a valid
$2$-sequence of $G$. It is accepted if $G$ has a proper $k$-coloring.
The binary language contains exactly the encodings of accepted instances.
The promise consists of the encodings of all instances, including negative ones.
-/

namespace Lax528502.ColoringInstances

open Lax228581.TwinWidth Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax759944.BinaryWordEncoding

/-- Write the RAM binary encoding over 2 symbols. A separator is 1, a zero
digit is 00, and a one digit is 01. These codewords form a prefix code. -/
def binary (words : List ℕ) : Word :=
  (encode words).flatMap fun s => match s with
    | .separator => [true]
    | .zero => [false, false]
    | .one => [false, true]

structure Instance where
  n : ℕ
  graph : SimpleGraph (Fin n)
  sequence : PartitionSequence graph 2
  colors : ℕ
  positive : 0 < colors

noncomputable def Instance.words (I : Instance) : List ℕ :=
  I.colors :: ContractionInput.encode (Equiv.refl _) I.graph I.sequence

noncomputable def Instance.bits (I : Instance) : Word := binary I.words

def wellFormed : Language := {w | ∃ I : Instance, I.bits = w}

def minimumColoring : Language :=
  {w | ∃ I : Instance, I.bits = w ∧ I.graph.Colorable I.colors}

end Lax528502.ColoringInstances

concepts.title: Reduction to Minimum Coloring with a 2-sequence
concepts.description:
The reduction of Section 5 turns disjoint directed paths in a DAG into
Minimum Coloring. Its cyclically arranged cliques have a polynomial-size
$2$-sequence which is included in the output. On every input, including a
negative input, the reduction returns a well-formed target instance.

The output is available both as a list of RAM words and under its binary
encoding for polynomial many-one reductions. A certificate for the target
language is a color for each vertex. The graph, sequence, and coloring can
all be checked in polynomial time.

import Lax528502.CliqueConstruction
import Lax759944.RamPolytime
import Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime

/-!
---
title: Reduction to Minimum Coloring with a 2-sequence
type: lemma
---
The reduction of Section 5 turns disjoint directed paths in a DAG into
Minimum Coloring. Its cyclically arranged cliques have a polynomial-size
$2$-sequence which is included in the output. On every input, including a
negative input, the reduction returns a well-formed target instance.

The output is available both as a list of RAM words and under its binary
encoding for polynomial many-one reductions. A certificate for the target
language is a color for each vertex. The graph, sequence, and coloring can
all be checked in polynomial time.
-/

namespace Lax528502.ColoringReduction

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialTime
open Lax759944.RamPolytime ColoringInstances

/-- The serialized clique graph carries a valid 2-sequence and is colorable
exactly when the specified directed paths exist. -/
axiom correct (I : DisjointPaths.Instance) : ∃ J : ColoringInstances.Instance,
    CliqueConstruction.words I=J.words ∧ (J.graph.Colorable J.colors ↔ I.Routable)

/-- The same reduction on the RAM and as a map on binary words. -/
axiom reduce :
    ∃ (ram : List ℕ → List ℕ) (f : Word → Word), RamPolytime ram ∧
      Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime id id f) ∧
      (∀ I : DisjointPaths.Instance, ram (I.bits.map Bool.toNat) = CliqueConstruction.words I) ∧
      ∀ x, (∃ I : ColoringInstances.Instance, ram (x.map Bool.toNat) = I.words ∧ f x = I.bits) ∧
        (x ∈ DisjointPaths.language ↔ f x ∈ minimumColoring)

/-- Verifying a supplied sequence and a coloring gives membership in NP. -/
axiom membership : minimumColoring ∈ NP

end Lax528502.ColoringReduction

concepts.title: Graphs with a supplied contraction sequence
concepts.description:
Number the vertices from $0$ to $n-1$. Write $n$ and the adjacency matrix of
the graph in row order. Append the number of merges and, for each partition
from the singletons to the last partition, its equivalence matrix in the same
order. An entry is $1$ precisely when the two vertices belong to the same part.
There are $n$ such matrices for a nonempty graph and 1 empty matrix for the
empty graph. The input thus has polynomial size in $n$ and does not depend on
a choice of names for the parts.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax228581.TwinWidth
import Mathlib.Data.List.OfFn

/-!
---
title: Graphs with a supplied contraction sequence
type: definition
---
Number the vertices from $0$ to $n-1$. Write $n$ and the adjacency matrix of
the graph in row order. Append the number of merges and, for each partition
from the singletons to the last partition, its equivalence matrix in the same
order. An entry is $1$ precisely when the two vertices belong to the same part.
There are $n$ such matrices for a nonempty graph and 1 empty matrix for the
empty graph. The input thus has polynomial size in $n$ and does not depend on
a choice of names for the parts.
-/

namespace Lax528502.ContractionInput

open Lax228581.TwinWidth

/-- The incidence matrix of a relation on numbered rows and columns. -/
noncomputable def matrix (m n : ℕ) (R : Fin m → Fin n → Prop) : List ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (List.ofFn fun i => List.ofFn fun j => if R i j then 1 else 0).flatten

/-- The graph alone, as a prefix of an instance with a contraction sequence. -/
noncomputable def graph {V : Type} {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V) (G : SimpleGraph V) : List ℕ :=
  n :: matrix n n (fun i j => G.Adj (order i) (order j))

/-- An explicit graph and its supplied partition sequence, in the given vertex order. -/
noncomputable def encode {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {n d : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V)
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G d) : List ℕ :=
  graph order G ++ ([S.stepCount] ++
    (List.range (S.stepCount + 1)).flatMap fun k =>
      matrix n n fun i j => ∃ B ∈ S.partition k, order i ∈ B ∧ order j ∈ B)

/-- The physical input convention of the polynomial-time word RAM. -/
def tape (x : List ℕ) : List ℕ := x.length :: x

end Lax528502.ContractionInput

concepts.title: Vertex-disjoint paths in directed acyclic graphs
concepts.description:
Given an acyclic digraph and a list of ordered pairs of distinct terminals,
decide whether there are pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths joining the
prescribed pairs. The number of pairs is part of the input. This problem is
NP-complete by Ganian, Hliněný, Kneis, Langer, Obdržálek, and Rossmanith,
Theorem 4.8(b). The vertices below are numbered in a topological order.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.ColoringInstances
import Lax429075.Reductions
import Mathlib.Data.List.Chain

/-!
---
title: Vertex-disjoint paths in directed acyclic graphs
type: theorem
---
Given an acyclic digraph and a list of ordered pairs of distinct terminals,
decide whether there are pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths joining the
prescribed pairs. The number of pairs is part of the input. This problem is
NP-complete by Ganian, Hliněný, Kneis, Langer, Obdržálek, and Rossmanith,
Theorem 4.8(b). The vertices below are numbered in a topological order.
-/

namespace Lax528502.DisjointPaths

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax429075.Reductions

structure Instance where
  n : ℕ
  arc : Fin n → Fin n → Prop
  forward : ∀ u v, arc u v → u < v
  terminals : List (Fin n × Fin n)
  nonempty : terminals ≠ []
  distinct : (terminals.flatMap fun p => [p.1, p.2]).Nodup

/-- The order and arc matrix, then the count of terminal pairs and the pairs. -/
noncomputable def Instance.bits (I : Instance) : Word :=
  ColoringInstances.binary (I.n :: ContractionInput.matrix I.n I.n I.arc ++
    [I.terminals.length] ++ I.terminals.flatMap fun (s, t) => [s.val, t.val])

def Instance.Routable (I : Instance) : Prop :=
  ∃ paths : Fin I.terminals.length → List (Fin I.n),
    (∀ i, (paths i).head? = some (I.terminals.get i).1 ∧
      (paths i).getLast? = some (I.terminals.get i).2 ∧ (paths i).IsChain I.arc) ∧
    ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (paths i).toFinset (paths j).toFinset

def language : Language := {w | ∃ I : Instance, I.bits = w ∧ I.Routable}

/-- The source problem for the coloring reduction. -/
axiom np_complete : NPComplete language

end Lax528502.DisjointPaths

concepts.title: Fringes and auxiliary partitions
concepts.description:
In a red path select the edges between two degree-2 parts. In a red cycle of
length at least 5 select every edge. Starting at a selected edge $BC$, trace
its unique red lift backwards until there is no lift, or an endpoint of the
lift has red degree 1. The fringe is empty in the first case and is that
endpoint in the second. Move the vertices of a fringe to the opposite part
of the selected edge.

Delete the selected edges from the red graph and group vertices according
to the component containing their receiving part. Every nonempty auxiliary
part has its cut covered by at most 4 chain subgraphs (Lemma 3.5).
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.ChainCuts
import Lax228581.TwinWidth

/-!
---
title: Fringes and auxiliary partitions
type: lemma
---
In a red path select the edges between two degree-2 parts. In a red cycle of
length at least 5 select every edge. Starting at a selected edge $BC$, trace
its unique red lift backwards until there is no lift, or an endpoint of the
lift has red degree 1. The fringe is empty in the first case and is that
endpoint in the second. Move the vertices of a fringe to the opposite part
of the selected edge.

Delete the selected edges from the red graph and group vertices according
to the component containing their receiving part. Every nonempty auxiliary
part has its cut covered by at most 4 chain subgraphs (Lemma 3.5).
-/

namespace Lax528502.Fringes

open Lax228581.TwinWidth

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-- The bipartite graph between two distinct parts of a 1-sequence is a chain graph. -/
axiom one_sequence (S : PartitionSequence G 1) (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ S.stepCount)
    (X Y : Finset V) (hX : X ∈ S.partition i) (hY : Y ∈ S.partition i) (hne : X ≠ Y) :
    ChainCuts.ChainOn G X Y

/-- Red adjacency at a partition. -/
def Red (P : Finset (Finset V)) (A B : Finset V) : Prop :=
  A ∈ P ∧ B ∈ P ∧ A ≠ B ∧ ¬ Homogeneous G A B

/-- The two other red neighbors are distinct and nonadjacent precisely in
the path and long-cycle cases of a red graph of maximum degree 2. -/
def Selected (P : Finset (Finset V)) (B C : Finset V) : Prop :=
  Red G P B C ∧ ∃ A D, Red G P A B ∧ Red G P C D ∧
    A ≠ C ∧ B ≠ D ∧ A ≠ D ∧ ¬ Red G P A D

/-- Red edges between earlier parts contained in the two current parts. -/
noncomputable def lifts (P : Finset (Finset V)) (B C : Finset V) : Finset (Finset V × Finset V) := by
  classical
  exact (P ×ˢ P).filter fun e => e.1 ⊆ B ∧ e.2 ⊆ C ∧ Red G P e.1 e.2

def Continues (P : Finset (Finset V)) (B C : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ e, lifts G P B C = {e} ∧ redDegree G P e.1 = 2 ∧ redDegree G P e.2 = 2

/-- The last earlier partition where tracing the unique degree-2 edge stops.
At that partition collect the endpoints of red degree 1. -/
noncomputable def fringe (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (i : ℕ) (B C : Finset V) : Finset V := by
  classical
  let stops := (Finset.range i).filter fun j => ¬ Continues G (S.partition j) B C
  exact if hs : stops.Nonempty then
    let P := S.partition (stops.max' hs)
    (lifts G P B C).biUnion fun e =>
      (if redDegree G P e.1 = 1 then e.1 else ∅) ∪ (if redDegree G P e.2 = 1 then e.2 else ∅)
  else ∅

/-- Each vertex is moved at most once, from the part containing it. -/
def Receives (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (i : ℕ) (v : V) (Q : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ P ∈ S.partition i, v ∈ P ∧
    ((Selected G (S.partition i) P Q ∧ v ∈ fringe G S i P Q) ∨
     (Q = P ∧ ¬ ∃ R, Selected G (S.partition i) P R ∧ v ∈ fringe G S i P R))

/-- Group the receivers by red connectivity after deleting selected edges. -/
noncomputable def auxiliary (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (i : ℕ) : Finset (Finset V) := by
  classical
  let P := S.partition i
  let remaining := fun A B => Red G P A B ∧ ¬ Selected G P A B
  let part := fun R => Finset.univ.filter fun v =>
    ∃ Q, Receives G S i v Q ∧ Relation.ReflTransGen remaining Q R
  exact (P.image part).erase ∅

/-- Every cut used in the auxiliary partitions has a cover by 4 chains. -/
axiom four_chains (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ S.stepCount)
    (X : Finset V) (hX : X ∈ auxiliary G S i) : Nonempty (ChainCuts.Cover G X 4)

end Lax528502.Fringes

concepts.title: Polynomial-time graph problems given a 2-sequence
concepts.description:
For every fixed $k$, a polynomial-time word RAM decides $k$-Coloring on graphs
supplied with a $2$-sequence. One can also find a minimum dominating, total
dominating, independent dominating, or connected dominating set, a minimum-weight
feedback vertex set, a minimum subset feedback vertex set, or a longest induced path.

These are Corollaries 1.2 and 3.11. They apply the algorithms of Bergougnoux,
Dreier, and Jaffke, Jaffke, Kwon, and Telle, and Bergougnoux, Papadopoulos,
and Telle to the branch decomposition of Theorem 1.1.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.ContractionInput
import Lax759944.RamPolytime
import Lax528502.GraphProblems

/-!
---
title: Polynomial-time graph problems given a 2-sequence
type: corollary
---
For every fixed $k$, a polynomial-time word RAM decides $k$-Coloring on graphs
supplied with a $2$-sequence. One can also find a minimum dominating, total
dominating, independent dominating, or connected dominating set, a minimum-weight
feedback vertex set, a minimum subset feedback vertex set, or a longest induced path.

These are Corollaries 1.2 and 3.11. They apply the algorithms of Bergougnoux,
Dreier, and Jaffke, Jaffke, Kwon, and Telle, and Bergougnoux, Papadopoulos,
and Telle to the branch decomposition of Theorem 1.1.
-/

namespace Lax528502.GraphAlgorithms

open Lax228581.TwinWidth Lax759944.RamPolytime GraphProblems

concepts.title: Domination, feedback vertex sets, and induced paths
concepts.description:
The objectives are minimum cardinality for domination and subset feedback
vertex set, minimum total weight for weighted feedback vertex set, and
maximum number of vertices for induced paths. An optimum is returned as a
vertex set. Weights and the set of marked vertices are part of the input.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.Vertex
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic

/-!
---
title: Domination, feedback vertex sets, and induced paths
type: definition
---
The objectives are minimum cardinality for domination and subset feedback
vertex set, minimum total weight for weighted feedback vertex set, and
maximum number of vertices for induced paths. An optimum is returned as a
vertex set. Weights and the set of marked vertices are part of the input.
-/

namespace Lax528502.GraphProblems

/-- The optimization problems and their additional instance data. Weights are
nonnegative integers in binary. A subset feedback vertex set hits every cycle
that visits a marked vertex. -/
inductive Problem (n : ℕ)
  | dominating | totalDominating | independentDominating | connectedDominating
  | weightedFeedback (weight : Fin n → ℕ)
  | subsetFeedback (marked : Finset (Fin n))
  | longestInducedPath

/-- Membership bits in vertex order. -/
def incidence {n : ℕ} (S : Finset (Fin n)) : List ℕ :=
  List.ofFn fun i => if i ∈ S then 1 else 0

/-- Problem tag and data following the graph and its sequence. -/
def Problem.words {n : ℕ} : Problem n → List ℕ
  | .dominating => [0]
  | .totalDominating => [1]
  | .independentDominating => [2]
  | .connectedDominating => [3]
  | .weightedFeedback w => 4 :: List.ofFn w
  | .subsetFeedback marked => 5 :: incidence marked
  | .longestInducedPath => [6]

def Dominates {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, v ∈ S ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj u v

/-- The set can be ordered as a path with no chords. -/
def InducesPath {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : List (Fin n), p ≠ [] ∧ p.Nodup ∧ p.toFinset = S ∧
    ∀ i j : Fin p.length, G.Adj (p.get i) (p.get j) ↔ i.val + 1 = j.val ∨ j.val + 1 = i.val

def Problem.Feasible {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) :
    Problem n → Prop
  | .dominating => Dominates G S
  | .totalDominating => ∀ v, ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj u v
  | .independentDominating => Dominates G S ∧ G.IsIndepSet (S : Set (Fin n))
  | .connectedDominating => Dominates G S ∧ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).Connected
  | .weightedFeedback _ => (G.induce {v | v ∉ S}).IsAcyclic
  | .subsetFeedback marked =>
      ∀ v, ∀ p : G.Walk v v, p.IsCycle → (∃ u ∈ p.support, u ∈ marked) →
        ∃ u ∈ p.support, u ∈ S
  | .longestInducedPath => InducesPath G S

/-- Compare two feasible vertex sets according to the selected objective. -/
def Problem.AtLeastAsGood {n : ℕ} (S T : Finset (Fin n)) : Problem n → Prop
  | .weightedFeedback w => S.sum w ≤ T.sum w
  | .longestInducedPath => T.card ≤ S.card
  | _ => S.card ≤ T.card

/-- Output 0 if infeasible, or 1 and the membership vector of an optimum. -/
def Problem.Answer {n : ℕ} (P : Problem n) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (out : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  (out = [0] ∧ ¬ ∃ S, P.Feasible G S) ∨
    ∃ S, out = 1 :: incidence S ∧ P.Feasible G S ∧
      ∀ T, P.Feasible G T → P.AtLeastAsGood S T

/-- Frame a graph instance and its accompanying problem data. -/
def input {n : ℕ} (x : List ℕ) (P : Problem n) : List ℕ := x.length :: x ++ P.words

end Lax528502.GraphProblems

concepts.title: Maximum induced matching width
concepts.description:
For a vertex set $X$, keep only the edges crossing from $X$ to its complement.
The cut value is the maximum size of an induced matching in this bipartite
graph. Adjacencies between two endpoints on the same side play no role.

Rooting a subcubic branch decomposition at an edge gives a binary tree whose
leaves are the vertices of the graph. Its width is the largest cut value below
a node. The mim-width of the graph is the minimum of these widths. The empty
graph has width $0$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax183560.BranchDecompositions
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Lattice.Fold
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Prod
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset

/-!
---
title: Maximum induced matching width
type: definition
---
For a vertex set $X$, keep only the edges crossing from $X$ to its complement.
The cut value is the maximum size of an induced matching in this bipartite
graph. Adjacencies between two endpoints on the same side play no role.

Rooting a subcubic branch decomposition at an edge gives a binary tree whose
leaves are the vertices of the graph. Its width is the largest cut value below
a node. The mim-width of the graph is the minimum of these widths. The empty
graph has width $0$.
-/

namespace Lax528502.MimWidth

open Lax183560

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- Pairs are oriented from the cut side to its complement. Between the two
endpoint sets, the only edges are the matching pairs themselves. -/
structure InducedMatching (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Finset V) (M : Finset (V × V)) : Prop where
  sides : ∀ e ∈ M, e.1 ∈ X ∧ e.2 ∉ X
  induced : ∀ e ∈ M, ∀ f ∈ M, G.Adj e.1 f.2 ↔ e = f

/-- The largest induced matching across a cut. -/
noncomputable def cutMim (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Finset V) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter (InducedMatching G X)).sup Finset.card

/-- A branch decomposition of width at most the specified bound. The empty
tree is available precisely when the vertex type is empty. -/
def Decomposes (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree V) → Prop
  | none => IsEmpty V
  | some T => T.Valid Finset.univ ∧ T.cutWidth (cutMim G) ≤ k

/-- The minimum width of a branch decomposition. -/
noncomputable def mimWidth (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ T, Decomposes G k T}

/-- Prefix notation for a branch tree. A fork is 0 and a leaf is its
vertex number plus 1. -/
def treeWord {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V) : BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree V → List ℕ
  | .leaf v => [(order.symm v).val + 1]
  | .fork l r => 0 :: treeWord order l ++ treeWord order r

/-- The empty list represents the empty decomposition. -/
def encode {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V) (T : Option (BranchDecompositions.BinaryTree V)) : List ℕ :=
  T.elim [] (treeWord order)

end Lax528502.MimWidth

concepts.title: The hierarchy of auxiliary parts
concepts.description:
Every part of the next auxiliary partition is a union of at most 5 parts of
the current partition. Keep a node when its part persists, and give every
new part the nodes of its constituent parts as children. Starting with the
singletons gives the rooted tree of Lemma 3.10. All its nodes are auxiliary
parts and it can be constructed in polynomial time.

import Lax528502.Fringes
import Lax528502.AuxiliaryTree

/-!
---
title: The hierarchy of auxiliary parts
type: lemma
---
Every part of the next auxiliary partition is a union of at most 5 parts of
the current partition. Keep a node when its part persists, and give every
new part the nodes of its constituent parts as children. Starting with the
singletons gives the rooted tree of Lemma 3.10. All its nodes are auxiliary
parts and it can be constructed in polynomial time.
-/

namespace Lax528502.PartitionHierarchy

open Lax228581.TwinWidth Lax759944.RamPolytime AuxiliaryTree

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- The old auxiliary blocks contained in the specified new block. -/
noncomputable def constituents (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (i : ℕ)
    (Y : Finset V) : Finset (Finset V) := by
  classical
  exact (Fringes.auxiliary G S i).filter (· ⊆ Y)

/-- The auxiliary partitions are nested under each contraction. -/
axiom refines (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < S.stepCount)
    (X : Finset V) (hx : X ∈ Fringes.auxiliary G S i) :
    ∃ Y ∈ Fringes.auxiliary G S (i+1), X ⊆ Y

/-- Each new block is the union of at most 5 old blocks. -/
axiom child_bound (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < S.stepCount)
    (Y : Finset V) (hy : Y ∈ Fringes.auxiliary G S (i+1)) :
    (constituents G S i Y).card ≤ 5 ∧ (constituents G S i Y).biUnion id = Y

/-- Leaves are the vertices, and each node records a part at a valid stage. -/
def FromPartitions {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (S : PartitionSequence G 2) : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V) → Prop
  | none => IsEmpty V
  | some h => h.refine.Valid Finset.univ ∧ h.All fun s =>
      ∃ i ≤ S.stepCount, s.support ∈ Fringes.auxiliary G S i

/-- The structural hierarchy, with all of its nodes witnessed by auxiliary parts. -/
axiom exists_tree (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2) : ∃ h, FromPartitions G S h

/-- The order, the number of stages, and the auxiliary equivalence matrices in stage order. -/
noncomputable def tables {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V) (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2) :
    List ℕ :=
  n :: (S.stepCount+1) :: (List.range (S.stepCount+1)).flatMap fun i =>
    ContractionInput.matrix n n fun a b => ∃ X ∈ Fringes.auxiliary G S i, order a ∈ X ∧ order b ∈ X

/-- A single polynomial-time RAM computes every auxiliary equivalence matrix. -/
axiom compute_partitions :
    ∃ build : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime build ∧
      ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V)
        (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2), build (ContractionInput.encode order G S) = tables order G S

axiom construct :
    ∃ build : List ℕ → List ℕ, RamPolytime build ∧
      ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V)
        (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2), ∃ h, FromPartitions G S h ∧
          build (ContractionInput.encode order G S) = AuxiliaryTree.encode order h

end Lax528502.PartitionHierarchy

concepts.title: Bags of the auxiliary tree
concepts.description:
Put $K=4(t-1)$. For an internal node with leaf set $X$ and children with
leaf sets $Y$, use the bag $H_X\cup\bigcup_Y I_Y$. Each leaf carries its
own vertex. The labels $H_X\cup I_X$ on the parent edges cover the cuts.
For each graph vertex their occurrences form a connected subtree containing
its leaf. In particular every graph edge has its ends together in a bag.

To compute $H_X$, enumerate subsets of $K+1$ neighbors of each outside
vertex and test independence. The sets $I_X$ then follow by scanning
adjacencies. This constructs the bags in $n^{O(t)}$ time (Section 4).
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax528502.AuxiliaryTree
import Lax808846.Ram

/-!
---
title: Bags of the auxiliary tree
type: lemma
---
Put $K=4(t-1)$. For an internal node with leaf set $X$ and children with
leaf sets $Y$, use the bag $H_X\cup\bigcup_Y I_Y$. Each leaf carries its
own vertex. The labels $H_X\cup I_X$ on the parent edges cover the cuts.
For each graph vertex their occurrences form a connected subtree containing
its leaf. In particular every graph edge has its ends together in a bag.

To compute $H_X$, enumerate subsets of $K+1$ neighbors of each outside
vertex and test independence. The sets $I_X$ then follow by scanning
adjacencies. This constructs the bags in $n^{O(t)}$ time (Section 4).
-/

namespace Lax528502.TreeBags

open AuxiliaryTree Lax228581.Treewidth Lax228581.TwinWidth Lax759944.RamPolytime Lax808846.Ram

variable {V : Type}

/-- Children in the order used to serialize the auxiliary tree. -/
def children : AuxiliaryTree.Tree V → List (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)
  | .leaf _ => []
  | .two a b => [a,b]
  | .three a b c => [a,b,c]
  | .four a b c d => [a,b,c,d]
  | .five a b c d e => [a,b,c,d,e]

/-- Nodes in preorder. A valid leaf labeling distinguishes all subtrees. -/
def subtrees : AuxiliaryTree.Tree V → List (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)
  | s@(.leaf _) => [s]
  | s@(.two a b) => s :: subtrees a ++ subtrees b
  | s@(.three a b c) => s :: subtrees a ++ subtrees b ++ subtrees c
  | s@(.four a b c d) => s :: subtrees a ++ subtrees b ++ subtrees c ++ subtrees d
  | s@(.five a b c d e) => s :: subtrees a ++ subtrees b ++ subtrees c ++ subtrees d ++ subtrees e

/-- Use a single node with an empty bag for the empty graph. -/
def nodes : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V) → List (Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V))
  | none => [none]
  | some s => (subtrees s).map some

/-- Tree adjacency, expressed on node labels. -/
def adjacent (x y : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)) : Prop :=
  match x, y with
  | some a, some b => b ∈ children a ∨ a ∈ children b
  | _, _ => False

variable [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- The union of the inside labels of the children. -/
noncomputable def childLabels (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
    (cs : List (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)) : Finset V :=
  (cs.map fun c => ChainCuts.inside G c.support k).foldr (· ∪ ·) ∅

noncomputable def bag (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V) → Finset V
  | none => ∅
  | some (.leaf v) => {v}
  | some s => ChainCuts.heavy G s.support k ∪ childLabels G k (children s)

/-- Node positions are the numbering used on the output tape. -/
abbrev Position (h : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)) := Fin (nodes h).length

/-- The concrete incidence matrices of the tree and its bags in preorder. -/
noncomputable def word {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V) (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
    (h : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)) : List ℕ :=
  let ns := nodes h
  ns.length :: ContractionInput.matrix ns.length ns.length (fun i j => adjacent (ns.get i) (ns.get j)) ++
    ContractionInput.matrix ns.length n (fun i j => order j ∈ bag G k (ns.get i))

/-- The stated bags on the specified tree form a tree decomposition of G. -/
axiom decomposition (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) (ht : 2 ≤ t)
    (hfree : TreeIndependence.InducedBicliqueFree G t)
    (h : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)) (hc : Certified G h) :
    ∃ (D : TreeDecomposition G) (number : Position h ≃ D.Node),
      (∀ i j, D.tree.Adj (number i) (number j) ↔ adjacent ((nodes h).get i) ((nodes h).get j)) ∧
      ∀ i, D.bag (number i) = bag G (4 * (t - 1)) ((nodes h).get i)

/-- Each canonical bag has independence number at most 84(t-1). -/
axiom bag_bound (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) (ht : 2 ≤ t)
    (hfree : TreeIndependence.InducedBicliqueFree G t)
    (h : Option (AuxiliaryTree.Tree V)) (hc : Certified G h) (i : Position h) :
    ∀ A ⊆ bag G (4 * (t - 1)) ((nodes h).get i), G.IsIndepSet (A : Set V) →
      A.card ≤ 84 * (t - 1)

/-- Construct a certified auxiliary tree and write its bags. The same
word RAM handles all values of the forbidden biclique size. -/
axiom compute :
    ∃ (p : Program) (c : ℕ), 0 < c ∧

concepts.description:
The independence number of a tree decomposition is the largest independence
number of one of its bags. Minimizing over all tree decompositions gives the
tree-independence number. An induced $K_{t,t}$ consists of 2 disjoint
independent sets of size $t$ with all edges between them present.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax228581.Treewidth
import Lax528502.ContractionInput
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique

/-!
---
title: Tree-independence number and induced bicliques
type: definition
---
The independence number of a tree decomposition is the largest independence
number of one of its bags. Minimizing over all tree decompositions gives the
tree-independence number. An induced $K_{t,t}$ consists of 2 disjoint
independent sets of size $t$ with all edges between them present.
-/

namespace Lax528502.TreeIndependence

open Lax228581.Treewidth

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- Exclusion of an induced complete bipartite graph with both sides of size t. -/
def InducedBicliqueFree (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ A B : Finset V, A.card = t ∧ B.card = t ∧ Disjoint A B ∧
    G.IsIndepSet (A : Set V) ∧ G.IsIndepSet (B : Set V) ∧
    ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ B, G.Adj a b

/-- Every independent subset of a bag has at most k vertices. -/
def BagBound {G : SimpleGraph V} (D : TreeDecomposition G) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, ∀ A ⊆ D.bag i, G.IsIndepSet (A : Set V) → A.card ≤ k

/-- Minimum over the independence bounds of the decompositions of G. -/
noncomputable def treeIndependenceNumber (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ∃ D : TreeDecomposition G, BagBound D k}

/-- Number of tree nodes, adjacency matrix of the tree, then the node-by-vertex
bag membership matrix. The choice of node numbering belongs to the producer. -/
noncomputable def encode {n m : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V} (order : Fin n ≃ V)
    (D : TreeDecomposition G) (nodes : Fin m ≃ D.Node) : List ℕ :=
  m :: ContractionInput.matrix m m (fun i j => D.tree.Adj (nodes i) (nodes j)) ++
    ContractionInput.matrix m n (fun i j => order j ∈ D.bag (nodes i))

end Lax528502.TreeIndependence

bag bound in $n^{O(t)}$ instructions (Theorem 4.1).

addition of $2$ includes the cases $n=0$ and $n=1$.

import Lax528502.TreeIndependence
import Lax808846.Ram

/-!
---
title: Tree-independence number of induced-biclique-free graphs of twin-width at most 2
type: theorem
---
Let $t\ge 2$. If $G$ has twin-width at most $2$ and contains no induced
$K_{t,t}$, its tree-independence number is at most $84(t-1)$. A word RAM
given $t$, $G$, and a $2$-sequence outputs a tree decomposition with this
bag bound in $n^{O(t)}$ instructions (Theorem 4.1).

One program and one absolute constant serve every $t$ and every graph order
$n$. A word width sufficient to address $(n+2)^{ct}$ cells suffices. The
addition of $2$ includes the cases $n=0$ and $n=1$.
-/

namespace Lax528502.TreeIndependenceBound

open Lax228581.TwinWidth Lax228581.Treewidth Lax808846.Ram TreeIndependence

/-- A single program constructs a tree and its bags in time n to an exponent
linear in t. The word-width threshold is fixed by the input parameters. -/
axiom construct :
    ∃ (program : Program) (c : ℕ), 0 < c ∧
      ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ V)
        (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : PartitionSequence G 2) (t : ℕ),
        2 ≤ t → InducedBicliqueFree G t →
        ∀ w : ℕ, (n + 2) ^ (c * t) < 2 ^ w →
          ∃ (D : TreeDecomposition G) (m : ℕ) (nodes : Fin m ≃ D.Node)
            (steps : ℕ), BagBound D (84 * (t - 1)) ∧ steps ≤ (n + 2) ^ (c * t) ∧
              RunsTo w program (ContractionInput.tape (t :: ContractionInput.encode order G S))
                (TreeIndependence.encode order D nodes) steps

/-- Excluding an induced biclique bounds the independence number of the bags. -/
axiom treeIndependence_le {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 2 ≤ t) (hfree : InducedBicliqueFree G t) (h : HasTwinWidthAtMost G 2) :
    treeIndependenceNumber G ≤ 84 * (t - 1)

end Lax528502.TreeIndependenceBound

proofs.description:
The hierarchy builder creates a node for each new auxiliary part. Apply
the chain-cover lemma at the partition stage where that part occurs.

Enumerate tuples of neighbors in base $n+2$. Test distinctness, adjacency,
and independence to determine the heavy and inside labels. Use the original
forks of the computed hierarchy to write the tree and bag matrices in preorder.
The tape, every intermediate value and every address fit in the stated word size.

An induced matching splits across a union of 2 cut sides. At a node with 5
children, the complement of 4 children consists of the first child and the
outside of the parent. This also gives a sum of at most 2 old cut values.

Construct the auxiliary tree, resolve its high-degree nodes, and write the
binary tree. On its prefix encoding the final RAM pass takes 4 instructions
per token plus 3 instructions for initialization and termination.

A crossing induced matching of size 2 cannot be contracted from singletons
to one part on each side. At the first merger uniting its two rows or its
two columns the resulting part would have two different red neighbors.

An oversized independent set in the heavy side supplies $t$ vertices in a
single chain. The smallest of their neighborhoods contains an independent
$t$-set, giving an induced biclique. On the inside, the largest light
neighborhood in each chain suffices to cover the corresponding endpoints.

Copies preserve the color order. Counting the inserted copies places a swap
or choice with left position p at column p+2 modulo k−1. The closing copies
make the number of columns equal to 1 modulo k−1.

A permutation that never decreases a position is the identity, since its
values have the same sum as the original positions. The choice gadget
allows just one decrease, from the right position of its pair to the left.
Exchanging these two positions removes that decrease. The extra edge of
the swap gadget rules out the identity.

Decode the input and certificate into native words. The verifier checks every
partition matrix, each two-part merge and every red degree, then checks the
vertex colors on all edges. Numbering the colors used by at most the order
of the graph gives a polynomial bound on certificate length.

At a cut, a bounded set of named vertices covers enough crossing edges
to keep every connected solution connected. Component labels of the
remaining outside graph record how its named vertices are joined.
The RAM checks the induced connectivity constraints on an auxiliary
graph using the archive's component search, and retains minimum witnesses.

Assign each edge of the matching to a chain that covers it. If two edges
were assigned to the same chain, nested neighborhoods would give a crossing
edge between their endpoints.

Reduce archive CNF satisfiability to disjoint paths. Each variable path
occupies one rail, and each clause must visit a literal on an unused rail.
For membership, give one path label per vertex. The verifier checks
successors against the directed adjacency matrix and the topological order.

The program reads the problem tag and returns a minimum witness. Each
tree table retains the best actual vertex set for each pair of sparse
neighborhood representatives on the two sides of the cut.

The RAM counts surviving marked edges and components before and after
removing the marked vertices. The cut certificates preserve their relative
cycle rank. Maximizing the binary weight of retained vertices minimizes
the weight of the returned deletion set. Unit weights give the minimum
subset feedback vertex set.

Every cut profile has a representative of size at most the cut mim-width.
A state gives one such representative for each color. A fixed polynomial
number of word-RAM rounds combines compatible child states over intervals
of the branch-tree word, including the empty graph and zero colors.

Each closed red component contributes one complete bipartite graph per part.
At a component incident with a selected edge, each of the central part's
two neighbors contributes one chain of core edges and one biclique for the
fringe or the endpoint. Together they cover every crossing graph edge.
Give the width-8 decomposition to the fixed-coloring algorithm.
Apply the corresponding bounded-mim-width algorithm with width 8.

Order siblings by their first vertex. Each earlier sibling on the path to
a vertex occupies twice its cardinality minus 1 words. Adding these
lengths and the intervening fork tags gives the absolute position of
every leaf and original fork. The remaining positions carry inserted forks.

At each stage put the constituent subtrees together in the order supplied by
the vertices. Retain a single child when a part persists. At the final stage
the root contains all vertices, and each genuine fork has 2 to 5 children.

Compose the reduction to disjoint paths on a DAG with the clique construction.
The latter supplies a 2-sequence on every output.
Combine the coloring verifier with the promise-preserving reduction.

The program reads the problem tag and invokes the corresponding
polynomial-time word RAM with the graph, its computed decomposition,
and any weights or marked vertices supplied on the tape.

Every old child has a representative whose parent lies in the new residual
component. Such a component has at most 4 parts, and only the merged part
has two preimages. Partition refinement gives the union equality.

Represent an old component by a part in it, taking the neighbor when the
part is a red leaf. Every old receiver moves to the new component of the
representative's parent. All representatives of one component agree there.

The RAM scans the supplied matrices for red edges and their degree-1
endpoints at the last stopping stage. Residual connectivity needs paths
of length at most 3. Each auxiliary matrix entry is a fixed counting term.

A connected graph is a path precisely when all degrees are at most 2
and some vertex has degree at most 1. Sparse representatives preserve
degrees truncated at 3 across a cut. The table maximizes the number
of selected vertices and returns their incidence vector.

A coloring of the padded cliques is equivalent to a successful routing of
the terminal colors. Growing block prefixes from right to left and then
merging consecutive blocks keeps every red degree at most 2.

The word RAM writes the padded cliques and all prefix partition matrices.
Counting expressions generate the transfers and padding in order. In each
merge phase a vertex changes its representative at most once. Binary parsing
and normalization extend the construction to malformed inputs.

At most 5 child labels contribute $4K$ each and the parent contributes $K$,
where $K=4(t-1)$. A leaf bag is a singleton.

Build the auxiliary tree, compute its bags, and use preorder for the node
numbering. The two incidence matrices on the output tape describe exactly the
tree and bags of the decomposition.

The parent-child graph on preorder nodes is a tree. Inside labels reach down
to their vertex's leaf. Heavy labels reach up to that leaf's branch, where
the sibling inequality connects them to an inside label. These paths connect
the occurrences of each vertex. For an edge, descend until its ends separate,
then use the cut labels to find a bag containing both ends.

Refine the tree of auxiliary parts to a binary tree. Its cuts witness the
bound in the minimum over branch decompositions.

Use the heavy-vertex and inside labels as bags on the auxiliary tree.
Their independence bounds witness the minimum over tree decompositions.
